# 3D drawings - Practice Test - Year 7

Attempt all questions and show your working. Suggested time: 30 to 35 minutes.

## Section A: Consolidating (Questions 1-4)

**Question 1**

How many faces, edges and vertices does a cube have?

**Question 2**

Name the solid that each net folds into.

(a) Six squares

(b) Two triangles and three rectangles

**Question 3**

A cylinder stands upright on a table. Describe the shape of:

(a) its top view

(b) its front view

**Question 4**

How many faces, edges and vertices does a square-based pyramid have?

## Section B: Standard (Questions 5-16)

**Question 5**

Describe the top view and the front view of each solid.

(a) A cone standing on its circular base

(b) A square-based pyramid standing on its base

**Question 6**

Copy and complete the table.

| Solid | Faces (F) | Vertices (V) | Edges (E) | F + V - E |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cube | 6 | 8 | 12 | ? |
| Triangular prism | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Square-based pyramid | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Hexagonal prism | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Pentagonal pyramid | ? | ? | ? | ? |

**Question 7**

A net is made of one hexagon and six identical triangles, with one triangle attached to each side of the hexagon. Name the solid it folds into.

**Question 8**

Isometric drawings are often drawn on triangular dot paper.

(a) In an isometric drawing of a box, which edges are drawn vertically, and which are drawn sloping?

(b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of an isometric drawing.

**Question 9**

A model is built from cubes stacked in columns on a table. Looking down from above, the columns sit in two rows of three. The numbers show how many cubes are in each column.

| | Left | Middle | Right |
|---|---|---|---|
| Back row | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| Front row | 1 | 1 | 0 |

(a) How many cubes are in the model?

(b) The front view is seen by looking at the model from the front. Write the height of the tallest column you would see in each position, from left to right.

(c) How many squares would the top view show?

**Question 10**

A set of three views (front, side and top) is often used to show an object. Give one advantage and one disadvantage of this kind of drawing.

**Question 11**

Will each net fold to make a cube? Answer yes or no.

(a) A row of four squares, with one extra square attached above the second square and one extra square attached below the second square.

(b) Six squares in one straight row.

(c) A row of four squares, with one extra square attached above the first square and one extra square attached below the fourth square.

**Question 12**

Name the shape of the cross-section in each case.

(a) A cylinder is sliced parallel to its circular base.

(b) A cube is sliced parallel to one of its faces.

(c) A square-based pyramid is sliced parallel to its base.

(d) A cone standing on its base is sliced straight down through its top point.

**Question 13**

In a perspective drawing of a long straight road, the two edges of the road seem to meet at a point on the horizon.

(a) What is this point called?

(b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of perspective drawings.

**Question 14**

Name the solid with each set of views.

(a) Front view: rectangle. Side view: rectangle. Top view: circle.

(b) Front view: triangle. Side view: triangle. Top view: circle.

(c) Front view: triangle. Side view: rectangle. Top view: rectangle.

**Question 15**

A net is made from two pentagons and five rectangles.

(a) Name the solid.

(b) How many faces, vertices and edges does it have?

**Question 16**

Which type of representation (net, three views, or perspective drawing) is most useful in each situation? Give a reason.

(a) A company needs to cut flat cardboard to make a box.

(b) A builder needs the exact measurements of each side of a shed.

(c) An advertisement shows how a new couch looks in a lounge room.

## Section C: Advanced (Questions 17-20)

**Question 17**

A solid has 12 vertices and 30 edges, and Euler's rule $F + V - E = 2$ holds for it. How many faces does it have?

**Question 18**

A large cube is made from $27$ small cubes, arranged $3$ by $3$ by $3$. The outside of the large cube is painted. How many small cubes have paint on:

(a) exactly $3$ faces

(b) exactly $2$ faces

(c) exactly $1$ face

(d) no faces

**Question 19**

Some cubes are stacked in columns on a $2$ by $2$ square base, with no gaps under any cube. The top view, the front view and the side view are each a $2$ by $2$ square.

(a) What is the largest number of cubes the model could have?

(b) What is the smallest number of cubes the model could have?

(c) What does this tell you about using only views to describe an object?

**Question 20**

A rectangular prism is built from $1 \text{ cm}$ cubes. It sits on a table, $4 \text{ cm}$ long from left to right, $3 \text{ cm}$ deep from front to back and $2 \text{ cm}$ high.

(a) How many cubes are used?

(b) Find the total surface area of the prism (the area of its net).

(c) Give the dimensions of the rectangle seen in the front view, the side view and the top view.
answers_md:
# 3D drawings - Answer Key

**Question 1**

Answer: $6$ faces, $12$ edges, $8$ vertices

**Question 2**

Answer: (a) cube (b) triangular prism

**Question 3**

Answer: (a) a circle (b) a rectangle

**Question 4**

Answer: $5$ faces, $8$ edges, $5$ vertices

**Question 5**

Answer: (a) top: a circle with a dot at its centre (the point); front: a triangle (b) top: a square with lines from each corner to the centre; front: a triangle

**Question 6**

Answer: Every row gives $F + V - E = 2$. Triangular prism $5, 6, 9$; square-based pyramid $5, 5, 8$; hexagonal prism $8, 12, 18$; pentagonal pyramid $6, 6, 10$

**Question 7**

Answer: a hexagonal pyramid

**Question 8**

Answer: (a) Vertical edges stay vertical; edges that are horizontal on the real box are drawn sloping at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. (b) Advantage: shows three faces at once with true lengths along the edges. Disadvantage: hidden faces or cubes cannot be seen (or it does not look as realistic as perspective).

**Question 9**

Answer: (a) $8$ (b) $3, 1, 2$ (c) $5$

**Question 10**

Answer: Advantage: shows the true shape and exact measurements of each face. Disadvantage: it is harder to picture the whole 3D object, and several drawings are needed.

**Question 11**

Answer: (a) yes (b) no (c) yes

**Question 12**

Answer: (a) circle (b) square (c) square (d) triangle

**Question 13**

Answer: (a) the vanishing point (b) Advantage: looks realistic, as the eye sees it. Disadvantage: lengths and angles are distorted, so true measurements cannot be read from it.

**Question 14**

Answer: (a) cylinder (b) cone (c) triangular prism

**Question 15**

Answer: (a) pentagonal prism (b) $7$ faces, $10$ vertices, $15$ edges

**Question 16**

Answer: (a) net (it shows the flat shape to cut and fold) (b) three views (they show true measurements of each side) (c) perspective drawing (it looks realistic)

**Question 17**

Answer: $20$ faces ($F = 2 - 12 + 30$)

**Question 18**

Answer: (a) $8$ (the corners) (b) $12$ (middle of each edge) (c) $6$ (centre of each face) (d) $1$ (the very centre)

**Question 19**

Answer: (a) $8$ (b) $6$ (two columns of $2$ on one diagonal, two columns of $1$ on the other) (c) Different objects can have the same views, so views alone may not show exactly how an object is built.

**Question 20**

Answer: (a) $24$ (b) $52 \text{ cm}^{2}$ ($2 \times (12 + 8 + 6)$) (c) front $4 \text{ cm}$ by $2 \text{ cm}$, side $3 \text{ cm}$ by $2 \text{ cm}$, top $4 \text{ cm}$ by $3 \text{ cm}$
